patterns.explanation_en: です is the polite copula used after nouns and な-adjectives. ます attaches to verb stems to form the polite present. Negative and past forms vary by part of speech: nouns / な-adjectives use じゃありません / でした; verbs use ません / ました.

examples.ja: わたしは がくせいです。
わたしは がくせいじゃありません。
あなたは がくせいですか。
きのうは やすみでした。
まいにち にほんごを べんきょうします。
私たちは がくせいです。
かれは がくせいです。
これは ほんです。
わたしは がくせいでは ありません。
まいにち えいがを みます。

common_mistakes.wrong: わたしは がくせいです じゃありません。
common_mistakes.right: わたしは がくせいじゃありません。
common_mistakes.why: Don't combine です and じゃありません. Use じゃありません alone for the polite negative of nouns / な-adjectives.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: わたしは いきますじゃありません。
common_mistakes.right: わたしは いきません。
common_mistakes.why: Verbs use ません for the polite negative, not じゃありません. じゃありません is only for nouns and な-adjectives.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: わたしが がくせいです。
common_mistakes.right: わたしは がくせいです。
common_mistakes.why: Self-introduction sentences declare the speaker AS THE TOPIC, so they use は (topic marker). が in the same slot would imply 'as for who the student is, it's me', answer to an unstated 'だれが学生ですか'. For a plain self-intro, は. (Note: 〜が is also correct here under a focus reading - it answers 'who?' / singles one out; 〜は is the neutral topic for a plain statement.)

contrasts.note: 〜です / 〜ます is the polite-form predicate ending. The topic-marker は usually pairs with です in introductory sentences (わたしは学生です). The two patterns work together: topic + polite predicate.
contrasts.native_reviewer_note: Pattern-instance contrast note verified by JLPT N5 specialist + native Japanese teacher review pass 2026-05-13

patterns.notes: Foundation pattern for all polite-form Japanese. Every other polite-form pattern in N5 builds on it.

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी SOV क्रम जापानी से मेल खाता है: यह आपकी ताक़त है। पर हिंदी में "है/हैं" वैकल्पिक नहीं, अनिवार्य है: जापानी です भी अनिवार्य है (केवल आकस्मिक भाषा में だ बन जाता है)। हिंदी में लिंग/वचन के अनुसार क्रिया बदलती है (खाता/खाती/खाते); जापानी क्रियाएँ कर्ता के लिंग/संख्या से नहीं बदलतीं: यह सरलता आपके पक्ष में है।

patterns.explanation_hi: です वाक्य के अंत में संज्ञा या な-विशेषण के बाद आता है: हिंदी के "है/हैं" के समान। ます क्रिया के स्तेम (मूल) में जुड़ने वाला विनम्र अंत्य है। यह जापानी विनम्र भाषा का सबसे बुनियादी रूप है। उदाहरण: 学生です = "विद्यार्थी हूँ/हैं"। 食べます = "खाता/खाती हूँ" (विनम्र)।

essay.intro: The polite-language ON switch. です = polite copula (after nouns / na-adjectives / sentence-end). ます = polite verb ending (replaces dictionary-form ending).
essay.why_it_matters: These are the foundation of polite Japanese. Master ~です/~ます and you can speak politely to anyone: bosses, strangers, customers. Drop them and you sound casual (only safe with friends/family). Knowing when to switch between the two registers IS the daily social muscle of Japanese.
essay.common_pitfalls: Mixing です with verb-form (×食べるです). Mixing です with i-adjective (the い is the verb-form: 高いです, NOT 高いだ). Forgetting past forms: でした (was) and ました (did).
essay.contrasts: vs Plain forms (~る, ~だ): same meanings, casual register. Use plain with friends/family; use polite with everyone else (default to polite as a learner).
essay.closing_practice_tip: Take a sentence you'd say to a friend (drop です/ます: 食べる) and re-cast it for a teacher (keep them: 食べます). Do this for 5 verbs and 5 noun sentences. The mental flick between casual and polite is the social muscle you're building.
essay.cultural_context: です/ます (polite affirmative) is the DEFAULT register in business, classrooms, customer-facing situations, and any first encounter. Switching to plain だ/だ.ない is reserved for close friends, family, internal thoughts, or written casual contexts. Mismatching the register is the single most common foreigner mistake. Typical contexts: formal_business, classroom, customer_service, first_meeting.

politeness_ladder.polite: です / 食べます
politeness_ladder.humble: 〜でございます (formal copula)
politeness_ladder.respectful: 〜でいらっしゃいます (about other)

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: わたし がくせい。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: わたしは がくせいです。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Polite predicate requires です; bare nouns are casual incomplete sentences.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: がっこうに いくます。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: がっこうに いきます。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Group-1 verb stem 行く→行き before ます (drop -u, add -i). Do not insert る.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: がくせいです か。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: がくせいですか。 (no space, falling tone often)
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: with rising tone. Question particle か attaches directly without space; spoken intonation can be flat or slightly rising.

patterns.explanation_en: は marks the TOPIC - what the sentence is about. The topic is usually given / known information. Pronounced 'wa' even though written with the kana は (ha). Often translated as 'as for ___' or simply omitted in English. Compare with が (subject), which often introduces NEW information.

examples.ja: わたしは がくせいです。
これは ほんです。
コーヒーは 飲みますが、にくは たべません。
examples.translation_en: I drink coffee, but I do not eat meat. (contrastive は: marks the contrast between two topics)
examples.note: Contrastive use of は - distinct from topic-marker は

examples.ja: あなたは にほんじんですか。
きのうは あめでした。
コーヒーは すきですが、おちゃは すきじゃありません。
examples.translation_en: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.

examples.ja: 私は 学生です。
これは ペンです。
にほんごは おもしろいです。
わたしは コーヒーを のみません。

common_mistakes.wrong: わたしわ がくせいです。
common_mistakes.right: わたしは がくせいです。
common_mistakes.why: The topic particle is always written with the kana は (ha) even though it's pronounced 'wa'. Don't write わ.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: わたしが がくせいです。
common_mistakes.right: わたしは がくせいです。
common_mistakes.why: は marks the TOPIC (already-known referent: わたし). が marks a new-information SUBJECT. For self-introduction (the referent わたし is automatically known to both speakers), は is required. Swapping to が shifts the sentence into a contrast or response-to-question reading. (Note: 〜が is also correct here under a focus reading - it answers 'who?' / singles one out; 〜は is the neutral topic for a plain statement.)

common_mistakes.wrong: 私が 学生です。
common_mistakes.right: 私は 学生です。
common_mistakes.why: Context: in self-introduction. は marks topic in introduction; が introduces NEW info or answers a who-question. (Note: 〜が is also correct here under a focus reading - it answers 'who?' / singles one out; 〜は is the neutral topic for a plain statement.)

contrasts.note: は marks the topic (often known); が marks the subject (often new information or focus).
は marks the topic of conversation; が marks subject (often the new/focused element). With existential verbs ある / いる, が marks what exists.

patterns.notes: は is the most-tested particle on JLPT N5. The は vs が distinction is the single most common source of N5 errors.

l1_notes.sov_advantage: हिंदी और जापानी दोनों SOV हैं - विषय-कर्म-क्रिया का क्रम समान है। यह संरचनात्मक लाभ है।
l1_notes.hi: हिंदी में "तो", "जी", "के बारे में" जैसे संकेतक हैं पर कोई बाध्य "विषय कण" नहीं। は और が का भेद हिंदी सीखने वालों के लिए सबसे बड़ी कठिनाई है। थंब-नियम: पहली बार किसी चीज़ का ज़िक्र हो → が; पहले से ज्ञात विषय पर बात हो → は। हिंदी "ने" कर्ता को मार्क करता है पर है vs है का भेद नहीं: जापानी में यह भेद ज़रूरी है।

essay.why_it_matters: は is the difference between "I am a student" (私は学生です, known topic) and "I, specifically, am the student" (私が学生です, new info). Beginners who default to が everywhere sound oddly emphatic. Mastering は means sounding NEUTRAL: the everyday, conversational baseline of Japanese.

essay.closing_practice_tip: Take any 5 sentences from your day and say each one in Japanese, deciding for each: "Is this a topic I'm introducing or one already in the conversation?" If introducing, use が; if continuing, use は. Repeat the drill at week 1, week 2, and month 1 to lock in the instinct.

Native speakers DROP は when the topic is obvious from context (most natural in casual speech: "コーヒー、好き？" instead of "コーヒーは好きですか？"). Over-use of は signals foreign-learner speech. Typical contexts: casual_conversation, classroom.

patterns.meaning_en: Subject marker - marks new information, focus, or the subject of certain stative verbs/adjectives

conjugations.label: Identifies / new information

Existence (with あります／います)
conjugations.example: へやに テレビが あります。

patterns.explanation_en: が marks the SUBJECT, especially when introducing new information or answering 'who/what?'. It is also REQUIRED with certain stative predicates: すき (like), きらい (dislike), わかる (understand), できる (can do), ほしい (want), あります／います (exist). Use が - never を - with these.

examples.ja: だれが きましたか。
にほんごが わかります。
ねこが すきじゃありません。
きのうは あめが ふりました。
へやに テレビが あります。
examples.translation_en: There is a TV in the room.

examples.ja: いぬが ほしいです。
だれが きょうしつに いますか。
ねこが います。
なにが おいしいですか。
やまださんが せんせいです。

common_mistakes.wrong: ねこを すきです。
common_mistakes.right: ねこが すきです。
common_mistakes.why: すき (like) takes が, never を - even though English uses 'I LIKE cats' with cats as the object. Same rule for きらい, わかる, できる, ほしい.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: わたしは がっこうの せんせいですか。
common_mistakes.right: だれが がっこうの せんせいですか。
common_mistakes.why: Context: when asking 'who is the teacher?'. Use が in question words like だれ／なに to ASK for new information. は can't introduce a new topic the listener doesn't know yet.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: だれは きましたか。
common_mistakes.right: だれが きましたか。
common_mistakes.why: Question-word subjects (だれが / なにが / どれが) ALWAYS take が, not は. Reason: は assumes the topic is known; question words are precisely what's NOT known. The answer also uses が: 田中さんが きました.

contrasts.note: が introduces new / focused information; は marks the already-known topic.

l1_notes.postposition_mapping: कर्ता-सूचक が को हिंदी ने (कर्ता-कारक का chiyno) से न मिलाएँ - जापानी が "नई जानकारी" या "स्थिति-क्रिया का कर्ता" मार्क करता है, जबकि हिंदी ने केवल पूर्ण काल में सकर्मक क्रिया के साथ आता है। これは何ですか। - それが本です। में が "वही चीज़ है" वाला ज़ोर देता है।
l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "ने" कर्ता को मार्क करता है (मैंने खाया), पर が से अलग है: "ने" केवल पूर्ण सकर्मक भूतकाल में आता है, が हर समय। हिंदी वक्ता अक्सर 好き के साथ を लगा देते हैं ("मुझे सेब पसंद है" → りんごを好き: गलत)। याद रखें: 好き/嫌い/上手/下手 से पहले हमेशा が, कभी を नहीं।

essay.why_it_matters: が picks out NEW information, the answer to a "who?" or "what?" question. Confusing は and が is the single biggest source of unnatural Japanese for beginners. essay.intro: This pattern, **を**, means: Direct object marker - marks the noun receiving the action of a transitive verb. At a glance: を marks the DIRECT OBJECT - the noun that receives the action. Used with transitive verbs (たべる, よむ, かう, みる, etc.). Pronounced 'o' (the same as お), but written with its own kana を. Also used with movement verbs to mark a path or route.
essay.why_it_matters: を marks the direct object: the thing being acted on. It also marks the path traversed (こうえんをあるく, walk through the park) and the point of departure (いえを出る, leave home). The transitive/intransitive split (見る/見える, あける/あく) is a daily decision; using を with an intransitive verb is one of the most-corrected errors.
essay.common_pitfalls: {'wrong': 'ともだちを あいました。', 'right': 'ともだちに あいました。', 'why': 'あう (to meet) is intransitive in Japanese - it takes に, not を. The person you meet is marked with に, not を.'} · {'wrong': 'にほんごを わかります。', 'right': 'にほんごが わかります。', 'why': 'わかる (to understand) takes が, not を. Same applies to すき, きらい, できる - they all take が.'}
essay.contrasts: Stative predicates like すき / わかる / できる take が, not を, even when English uses an object.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 5 transitive-verb sentences using を today, then convert each to its intransitive counterpart (no を, use が). Example: ドアをしめます → ドアがしまります. This drills the transitivity-pair vocabulary and forces you to feel which verb takes を.
essay.cultural_context: を (direct object) is often dropped in casual speech ("ごはん食べる？" instead of "ごはんを食べる？"). Foreign learners cling to it; native casual speech is more elliptical. Keep を in formal/written contexts and when ambiguity threatens. Typical contexts: casual_drop, formal_keep.

wrong_corrected_pair.why: を marks the direct object; に would mean "to/for the pizza".

patterns.explanation_en: に has four core uses at N5: (1) location of EXISTENCE with ある／いる, (2) specific point in TIME (7時に, げつようびに), (3) DESTINATION with movement verbs (いく, くる, かえる), (4) RECIPIENT of giving / sending verbs (あげる, おくる, でんわする). Compare carefully with で (location of ACTION) and へ (purely directional).

examples.ja: 7時に おきます。
にほんに いきません。
へやに なにが ありますか。
ともだちに ほんを あげました。
examples.translation_en: I gave a book to my friend.

examples.ja: うちに かえります。
ねこは いすに います。
examples.translation_en: The cat is on/by the chair.

examples.ja: 父に てがみを かきます。
examples.translation_en: I write a letter to my father.

examples.ja: がっこうに いきます。
はちじに おきました。
ともだちに あいました。

common_mistakes.wrong: としょかんに ほんを よみます。
common_mistakes.right: としょかんで ほんを よみます。
common_mistakes.why: Location of an ACTION (where you do something) takes で. Location of EXISTENCE takes に. Reading is an action, so use で.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: あした に いきます。
common_mistakes.right: あした いきます。
common_mistakes.why: Relative time words (あした, きょう, きのう, いま, まいにち) DON'T take に. Only specific clock / calendar times do (7時に, げつようびに, 4月に).
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: 7時で おきます。
common_mistakes.right: 7時に おきます。
common_mistakes.why: Specific clock times take に (に for absolute/point-in-time markers). で marks the LOCATION of an action (としょかんで べんきょうします), not the TIME. Don't confuse: で = where; に = when (for specific clock times / dates / days-of-week).

contrasts.note: に = location of existence; で = location of action. へやに ねこが います (the cat IS in the room) vs へやで ねこと あそびます (I PLAY with the cat in the room).
に = destination (general, also covers existence/time/recipient); へ = direction (purely movement-toward, slightly more formal).

patterns.notes: The に vs で distinction (existence vs action) is a top-3 N5 error source. Always ask: is the verb stative (ある／いる) or active (する／たべる／よむ)?

l1_notes.postposition_mapping: に के अनेक प्रयोग हिंदी में अलग-अलग पदसर्ग बनाते हैं: समय → -बजे / पर / को (3時に = 3 बजे), स्थान-अस्तित्व → में / पर (ここにある = यहाँ है), दिशा → की ओर / को (東京に行く = टोक्यो जाना), अप्रत्यक्ष कर्ता → को (彼にあげる = उसे देना)। हिंदी से (= "से") में से अधिकांश に से नहीं で या から होता है।
l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "में" का जापानी समकक्ष संदर्भ-निर्भर है: स्थिर अस्तित्व → に (家にいる = "घर में हूँ"); गति की क्रिया → に (家に帰る = "घर लौटता हूँ"); पर कार्य उस स्थान पर हो रहा हो → で (家で食べる = "घर में खाता हूँ")। समय के "में" → に (七時に)। हिंदी वक्ता अक्सर हर "में" के लिए に लगा देते हैं: कार्य के स्थान पर で आना भूल जाते हैं। यह जापानी सीखने में सबसे आम गलती है।

l1_notes.postposition_mapping: で की दो भूमिकाएँ हिंदी में अलग-अलग पदसर्ग हैं: क्रिया-स्थान → में / पर (図書館で勉強する = पुस्तकालय में पढ़ाई करना), साधन → से (ペンで書く = पेन से लिखना)। हिंदी से दोनों रूप व्यक्त करता है - जापानी में में-वाला से = で, से-वाला से = で (साधन)।

essay.why_it_matters: で is the "where the action happens" particle (こうえんであそぶ) AND the "instrument/means" particle (えんぴつで書く / 電車で来る). One particle covers two grammatically distinct concepts. Mistaking で for に in the location-of-existence sense (いる/ある needs に) is the single biggest beginner error.

essay.intro: This pattern, **と**, means: With (companion) / and (exhaustive listing) / quotation marker. At a glance: と has three N5 uses: (1) WITH a person (ともだちと あう), (2) AND for listing nouns EXHAUSTIVELY - only these and nothing else (パンと コーヒー), and (3) QUOTATION marker before いう (say) or おもう (think). essay.why_it_matters: と does double duty: "with X" (companion) and "X and Y and Z" (exhaustive listing). The exhaustive listing is the catch: や is for non-exhaustive ("X and Y, among others"). Get this wrong and you're telling Japanese listeners "these are literally the only items," when you meant "things like X and Y."

patterns.explanation_en: から has two roles at N5: (1) FROM - a starting point in time or place, attaching to a noun (9時から, とうきょうから), and (2) BECAUSE - attaching to a full clause (plain or polite form), giving the reason for what follows. Often paired with まで (until). The 'because' use commonly precedes a request or command.

common_mistakes.wrong: あつい です から、まどを あけてください。
common_mistakes.right: あついから、まどを あけてください。 (or あついですから、〜)
common_mistakes.why: い-adjectives attach から directly (あついから). Don't insert です between them. Polite form あついですから is grammatical but stylistically less natural.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.right: がっこうへ いって、ともだちに あいます。 (sequential) - OR - ともだちに あうから、がっこうへ いきます。 (because)
common_mistakes.why: から (because) connects REASON → result. The reason clause comes first. If you're listing sequential actions, use the て-form, not から.

common_mistakes.right: 9時から しごとです。
common_mistakes.why: から marks the STARTING point ('from 9'). で would mean 'at 9' as a location/event (9時で会議 = the meeting is at 9). For a time RANGE ('from X to Y'), pair から with まで: 9時から 5時まで しごとです.

contrasts.note: から (from time/place) is often paired with まで (until time/place): 9時から 5時まで = from 9 to 5.
から (informal/causal) and ので (formal/objective) both mean "because"; から for spoken/casual, ので for written/polite.

patterns.notes: Note ので is a softer, more polite alternative for 'because' (Upper N5 / borderline).

essay.intro: This pattern, **から**, means: From (starting point in time / place) / because (reason). At a glance: から has two roles at N5: (1) FROM - a starting point in time or place, attaching to a noun (9時から, とうきょうから), and (2) BECAUSE - attaching to a full clause (plain or polite form), giving the reason for what follows. Often paired with まで (until)...
essay.why_it_matters: から marks the STARTING POINT: of time, place, or causation. The same particle does triple duty: 9時から (from 9 o'clock), とうきょうから (from Tokyo), さむいから (because it's cold). The causation use is what makes Japanese explanations feel cumulative: the reason precedes the result.

The reason clause comes first. If you're listing sequential actions, use the て-form, not から."}
essay.contrasts: から (from time/place) is often paired with まで (until time/place): 9時から 5時まで = from 9 to 5. · から (informal/causal) and ので (formal/objective) both mean "because"; から for spoken/casual, ので for written/polite.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build a one-day schedule sentence: 9時から12時までしごとをします (I work from 9 to 12). Then add a reason: つかれたから、休みます (I'm tired, so I'll rest). Practice the time-from / cause-from pairing in 5 different sentences.
essay.cultural_context: から as "from" (location/time) is straightforward; から as "because" requires the speaker to take a position. ので is softer for the same meaning: use ので in business / apologies / formal writing. Typical contexts: reason_giving, time_range.

essay.intro: This pattern, **まで**, means: Until / up to (a point in time or place); often paired with から. At a glance: まで marks the END of a span - until a time, up to a place. essay.intro: This pattern, **や**, means: And - non-exhaustive listing (these and others). At a glance: や lists nouns NON-EXHAUSTIVELY - A, B, and others (implied). Often paired with など (etc.) at the end of the list. Contrast with と, which is EXHAUSTIVE - only A and B and nothing else.
essay.why_it_matters: や signals "X, Y, and other things like that". This is the everyday, low-key way Japanese speakers list: claiming an exhaustive と-list usually feels too formal or oddly precise.

essay.contrasts: や = non-exhaustive (and others). と = exhaustive (only these). Pick based on whether 'etc.' is implied.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Describe what you ate today using や: あさはパンやコーヒーやくだものなどを食べました (for breakfast I had bread, coffee, fruit, and so on). Add など at the end to reinforce the "and others" sense.
essay.cultural_context: や (non-exhaustive list) is the conversational equivalent of "...and that kind of thing". "本や雑誌があります" implies more than just books and magazines. The exhaustive と is when you want to be explicit. Native speakers default to や. Typical contexts: casual_description.

wrong_corrected_pair.why: When や ends a list, add など or another connector before the verb. Bare や cannot directly attach to を.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: りんごや みかんと バナナを かいました。

wrong_corrected_pair.why: Mix of や and と is wrong. と is exhaustive ("just A and B"); や is non-exhaustive ("A, B, etc.").

essay.intro: This pattern, **も**, means: Also / too / even (with negation: 'not even / no one / nothing'). At a glance: も means 'also/too/even'. It REPLACES は, が, or を: わたしも (NOT わたしはも). It STACKS after other particles: にも, でも, とも, からも. With negative verbs and question words like だれ/なに, it forms 'no one / nothing': だれも きませんでした (no one came).
essay.why_it_matters: も replaces the marker (は/が/を) it inherits, NOT stack with it. 私もです, not 私はもです. Same with negation: 何もありません (nothing at all) vs 何かあります (something does). The double-no rule (も + negative = nothing/no one/nowhere) is a closed-system pattern worth memorising.

But it STACKS after に, で, と, etc.: とうきょうにも is correct.'} · {'wrong': 'だれも きました。', 'right': 'だれも きませんでした。 (no one came) / みんな きました。 (everyone came)', 'why': "だれも with an AFFIRMATIVE verb is ungrammatical. To say 'everyone' use みんな. だれも only works with negative verbs to mean 'no one'."}
essay.contrasts: も = "also/too" (additive on the same role); と = "with/and" (comitative or A+B exhaustive listing).
essay.closing_practice_tip: Make 5 negative sentences using question-word + も: だれも来ません, 何もありません, どこも行きません, etc. Note how each "nothing" depends on a single も sitting between the question word and the negative verb.
essay.cultural_context: も (also/too) attaches to a noun and replaces other particles ("私もです" not "私はもです"). With negation, "誰も〜ない" / "何も〜ない" / "どこも〜ない" form total-negation idioms ("no one", "nothing", "nowhere"): these are textbook drill points. Typical contexts: similar_to_previous, total_negation.

patterns.explanation_en: The こ/そ/あ/ど pronouns refer to OBJECTS (or abstract things). これ = near speaker, それ = near listener, あれ = far from both, どれ = which one (question). They stand alone - DON'T put a noun after them. For 'this book' use この, not これ.

patterns.pattern: この／その／あの／どの ＋ N (noun)
patterns.meaning_en: Adjective form: this / that / which + Noun (always followed by a noun)
patterns.meaning_ja: 「この・その・あの・どの」+ めいし で、ものを 「これ」と さして いいます。「この本」「その本」「あの本」「どの本」。

conjugations.label: this + N (near speaker)
conjugations.example: この ほんを よみます。

conjugations.label: that + N (near listener)
conjugations.example: その ペンは あなたのですか。

conjugations.label: that + N (far)
conjugations.example: あの くるまは だれのですか。

conjugations.label: which + N (question)
conjugations.example: どの ねこが すきですか。

patterns.explanation_en: Use この/その/あの/どの directly before a noun. Mirrors これ/それ/あれ/どれ exactly but ALWAYS followed by a noun: この ほん = 'this book', あの 人 = 'that person'.

examples.ja: この ほんを よみました。
その ペンは あなたのですか。
あの 人は だれですか。
どの くるまが いいですか。
この みせは あまり たかくないです。
あの ねこは どこから 来ましたか。
examples.translation_en: Where did that cat come from?

examples.ja: どの えいがを 見ますか。
この ほんは おもしろいです。
その ペンは だれの ですか。
あの くるまは はやいです。

common_mistakes.wrong: これの ほんを よみます。
common_mistakes.right: この ほんを よみます。
common_mistakes.why: Don't write これの ほん. Use この directly before a noun. これ + noun is wrong - それ is for 'that pronoun', この is for 'this + noun'.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: この。
common_mistakes.right: この + (a noun) - always.
common_mistakes.why: この/その/あの/どの can NEVER stand alone - they MUST be followed by a noun. If standing alone, use これ/それ/あれ/どれ.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: これ ほんを よみました。
common_mistakes.right: この ほんを よみました。
common_mistakes.why: これ is a STANDALONE pronoun ('this thing'). この is a NOUN-MODIFIER ('this [noun]'). Before a noun, use この/その/あの/どの. Without a noun, use これ/それ/あれ/どれ. Common N5 error: skipping the の of この.

contrasts.note: この + N = 'this + N'. これ alone = 'this' (pronoun).

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "यह / वह" विशेषण और सर्वनाम दोनों रूप में काम कर सकता है (यह किताब / यह है)। जापानी में यह काम के अनुसार बँटा है: संज्ञा को संशोधित करना (विशेषण-रूप) → この/その/あの/どの; अकेले खड़ा (सर्वनाम-रूप) → これ/それ/あれ/どれ। हिंदी वक्ताओं की सबसे आम ग़लती: これ本 (ग़लत) → この本 (सही)।

patterns.meaning_hi: विशेषण रूप: यह / वह / कौन सा + संज्ञा
patterns.explanation_hi: この / その / あの / どの: विशेषण रूप; अनिवार्य रूप से संज्ञा के साथ आने चाहिए (この本 = "यह किताब", これ本 ग़लत)। दूरी-नियम वही: इन्हें सर्वनाम (これ/それ/अरे/どれ) से अलग करना ज़रूरी।

essay.intro: Adjectival demonstratives that ALWAYS attach directly to a noun: この本 (this book), その人 (that person near you), あの店 (that shop over there), どのカバン (which bag).
essay.why_it_matters: These look identical in meaning to これ/それ/あれ/どれ but grammatically must take a noun. Mixing up the two systems (using これ as a determiner: ×これ本) is the most-corrected error among English-speaking learners. The kosoado split itself (near-speaker / near-listener / far / which) is unique to Japanese and worth memorising as a system.
essay.common_pitfalls: Using これ/それ/あれ/どれ in front of a noun (×これ ペン → must be このペン). Forgetting the listener-relative middle term: その is what's near the OTHER person, not what's far from both.
essay.contrasts: vs これ/それ/あれ/どれ: pronouns standing alone vs. determiners attached to nouns. Same kosoado split, different grammar slot.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Stand somewhere with 3 objects at different distances. Point at each and say two sentences for each: a pronoun-only one (「これは ペンです」) and a determiner-plus-noun one (「このペンは 高いです」). The body memory locks in which form goes where.
essay.cultural_context: この/その/あの/どの (demonstrative determiners) attach DIRECTLY before a noun and never carry a particle: "この本" not "このの本". Most learners over-apply の after possessives and instinctively insert it here too. Skip the の. Typical contexts: describing_objects, pointing.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: この は ほんです。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: これは ほんです。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: intent: this is a book. この must be followed by a noun (この + N). For "this (alone)" use これ.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: この ほんが わたし の です。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: この ほんは わたしのです。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: When introducing a topic ("As for this book, it is mine"), use は, not が.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: そのほん。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: その ほん。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: no spacing. Wakachi spacing: separate determiner from noun in early-N5 reading.

authentic_citations.context: Pre-nominal determiners: この本 / その人 etc.
コソアド: noun-modifying row (must attach to noun).

politeness_ladder.casual: この ほん、おもしろい。
politeness_ladder.polite: この ほんは おもしろいです。
politeness_ladder.humble: こちらの ほんは おもしろうございます。
politeness_ladder.respectful: こちらの ほんを ごらんに なって ください。

cultural_callout.note: この/その/あの/どの (demonstrative determiners) attach DIRECTLY before a noun and never carry a particle: "この本" not "このの本". Most learners over-apply の after possessives and instinctively insert it here too. Skip the の.

patterns.meaning_en: Location words: here / there-near-listener / over-there / where
patterns.meaning_ja: ばしょの ことば

conjugations.label: Here (near speaker)
conjugations.example: ここは としょかんです。

conjugations.label: There (near listener)
conjugations.example: そこに ねこが います。

conjugations.label: Over there (far from both)
conjugations.example: あそこへ いきましょう。

conjugations.label: Where (question)
conjugations.example: どこで かいましたか。

patterns.explanation_en: Same こ/そ/あ/ど logic but for LOCATIONS. Take は, が, に, で, から, まで etc. as needed. ここ/そこ/あそこ are statements; どこ asks 'where?'. With も + negative: どこにも いきません = 'I'm going nowhere'.

examples.ja: ここは としょかんです。
そこに ねこが います。
どこで かいましたか。
あそこは しずかです。
どこにも いきません。
ここで まちます。
ホテルは あそこです。
ここは わたしの きょうしつです。
そこに ペンが あります。
あそこに ぎんこうが あります。

common_mistakes.wrong: ここに ねこは あります。
common_mistakes.right: ここに ねこが います。
common_mistakes.why: Use います for animate things (people, animals); あります is only for inanimate things.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: これは としょかんです。
common_mistakes.right: ここは としょかんです。
common_mistakes.why: ここ/そこ/あそこ/どこ are PLACES; これ/それ/あれ/どれ are THINGS. For 'this place is the library' use ここ, not これ.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Fixed 2026-05-31 per native-review false-negative report (BUG-247): the previous form was correct Japanese; reframed. Pending native confirmation.

common_mistakes.wrong: あそこは としょかんです。
common_mistakes.right: ここは としょかんです。
common_mistakes.why: ここ marks the SPEAKER'S CURRENT LOCATION ('here, where I am'). あそこ would be 'over there, far from us'. For introducing the speaker's surrounding building, use ここ.

contrasts.note: The ここ-series = LOCATIONS. The これ-series = OBJECTS. Don't mix them: 'here is a book' = ここに ほんが あります, NOT これに ほんが あります.

patterns.explanation_hi: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ: स्थान-शब्द। दूरी-नियम वही: ここ = "यहाँ" (वक्ता-निकट); そこ = "वहाँ" (श्रोता-निकट); あそこ = "उधर" (दोनों से दूर, ध्यान दें: あこ नहीं, あそこ); どこ = "कहाँ"। प्रयोग: ここはトイレです = "यहाँ शौचालय है"; ここで食べる = "यहाँ खाता हूँ"।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी में "यहाँ / वहाँ / कहाँ" तीन हैं; जापानी में चार (पाँच यदि どちら जोड़ें)। हिंदी "वहाँ" अस्पष्ट है: श्रोता-निकट? दूर? जापानी में स्पष्ट: श्रोता के पास → そこ; दूर → あそこ। फ़ोन पर: "वहाँ ठंड है?", यदि "आपके वहाँ" → そちら / そこ; यदि किसी और जगह → あちら / あそこ।

essay.intro: This pattern, **ここ／そこ／あそこ／どこ**, means: Location words: here / there-near-listener / over-there / where. At a glance: Same こ/そ/あ/ど logic but for LOCATIONS. Take は, が, に, で, から, まで etc. as needed. ここ/そこ/あそこ are statements; どこ asks 'where?'. With も + negative: どこにも いきません = 'I'm going nowhere'.
essay.why_it_matters: Place-version of the kosoado system. Same near/medium/far/which logic but applied to LOCATIONS. ここ ≠ here in English (it includes "where the speaker is"); としょかんはあそこです vs としょかんはそこです changes the listener's mental map.
essay.common_pitfalls: {'wrong': 'ここに ねこは あります。', 'right': 'ここに ねこが います。', 'why': 'Use います for animate things (people, animals); あります is only for inanimate things.'} · {'wrong': "どこも しずかです。 (with affirmative - meaning 'every place is quiet')", 'right': "どこも しずかです。 IS valid - but watch the rule: どこも + AFFIRMATIVE = 'everywhere'; どこも/どこにも + negative = 'nowhere'.", 'why': "Polarity flip: question word + も + affirmative = 'every', + negative = 'no'. Same rule applies to だれも, なにも, いつも."}
essay.contrasts: The ここ-series = LOCATIONS. The これ-series = OBJECTS. Don't mix them: 'here is a book' = ここに ほんが あります, NOT これに ほんが あります.
essay.closing_practice_tip: In any conversation today (or imagined), use here/there/over-there in the right slot. Bonus: ask どこですか three times for genuinely unknown locations and notice how the answer always uses one of the other three.
essay.cultural_context: ここ/そこ/あそこ/どこ (place pronouns) use the same proximity rule as これ/それ/あれ. あそこ ("over there") is most idiomatic when both speaker and listener can see the place: if it's only known to one of you, それ vs こちら applies depending on register. Typical contexts: directions, meeting_points.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: ここ は ぎんこうですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: ここは ぎんこうですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Spacing: は attaches directly to ここ; do not insert a space.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: どこは ぎんこうですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: ぎんこうは どこですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Question word どこ takes が, but typical phrasing is "X は どこ ですか" (where is X), not "どこは X ですか".

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: こちらは どこ ですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: ここは どこ ですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: asking your own location. こちら is polite/direction ("this way / over here"); ここ is the spatial pronoun ("here").

authentic_citations.context: Location pronouns: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ.
コソアド: place row, often appears in は〜ですか questions.

politeness_ladder.polite: ここは いいですね。
politeness_ladder.humble: こちらは いいところで ございますね。
politeness_ladder.respectful: こちらは いい ところで いらっしゃいますね。

cultural_callout.note: ここ/そこ/あそこ/どこ (place pronouns) use the same proximity rule as これ/それ/あれ. あそこ ("over there") is most idiomatic when both speaker and listener can see the place: if it's only known to one of you, それ vs こちら applies depending on register.

patterns.meaning_en: What - pronounced なに or なん depending on what follows
patterns.meaning_ja: 「何（なに／なん）」は きく ときの ことばです。よみかたは ふたつ あります。「なに」と「なん」、どちらも かんじは「何」です。「なに」は ものを きく とき。「なん」は かずや「です」の まえで。

conjugations.label: なに + を, が, も, は
conjugations.example: なにを たべますか。

conjugations.label: なん + です, でしょう, だ
conjugations.example: これは なんですか。

conjugations.label: なん + counter (じ, にん, さい...)
なんで (how / why; informal)
conjugations.example: なんで きましたか。

patterns.explanation_en: なに and なん both mean 'what'. The pronunciation depends on what follows: なん before です, ですか, でしょう, and counters (なんじ, なんにん, なんさい); なに before を, が, も, は. Memorize the pattern. なんで means 'how/why' (informal); なぜ is the formal 'why'.

examples.ja: なにを たべますか。
これは 何ですか。
いま なんじですか。
なにが すきですか。
何（なに）で 来ましたか。
examples.translation_en: How (by what means) did you come?

examples.ja: なんで 行きますか。
examples.translation_en: By what means do you go?

examples.ja: なんさいですか。
これは なんですか。
なにを かいますか。

common_mistakes.wrong: なんを たべますか。
common_mistakes.right: なにを たべますか。
common_mistakes.why: なに before を (and が, も). Never なん before を. The trigger for なん is です / ですか / でしょう / counters.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: なにじですか。
common_mistakes.right: なんじですか。
common_mistakes.why: Counters always trigger なん: なんじ, なんにん, なんさい, なんがつ, なんにち, なんようび.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: なにが たべますか。
common_mistakes.right: なにを たべますか。
common_mistakes.why: なに is the direct OBJECT of たべる (eat), so it takes を, not が. が would put なに in the subject slot (asking 'what eats?': nonsense). The direct-object rule: transitive verb + を + object.

contrasts.note: 何 asks about things; だれ asks about people. Both follow the question-word rule: in subject position they take が (not は) because the question word is precisely the new-information slot.
contrasts.native_reviewer_note: Pattern-instance contrast note verified by JLPT N5 specialist + native Japanese teacher review pass 2026-05-13

patterns.meaning_hi: क्या - आगे आने वाले शब्द से なに/なん उच्चारण
patterns.explanation_hi: 何 दो उच्चारण रखता है: なに या なん, पीछे आने वाले शब्द से तय होता है। /d/, /n/, /t/ या गणना से पहले → なん (なんですか, なんにん, 何時); अन्य ध्वनियों से पहले → なに (何を, 何が, 何で)। N5 का सबसे मूल प्रश्न-शब्द।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "क्या" वाक्य के शुरू में आ सकता है ("क्या आप जापानी हैं?"); जापानी में 何 + か सिर्फ़ "क्या" है, और か (प्रश्न-कण) वाक्य के अंत में आता है। हिंदी वक्ता अक्सर 何 को वाक्य के शुरू में लगा देते हैं: जापानी में 何 अपनी प्राकृतिक स्थिति में रहता है (आम तौर पर बीच में)। उच्चारण भेद याद रखना ज़रूरी: 何時 (नान-जि, "क्या समय") vs 何を (नानि-ओ, "क्या-को")।

essay.intro: Two readings of the same kanji 何, used in different contexts. なに is the stand-alone question (何ですか?). なん appears before counters (何時 nanji, 何人 nannin) and certain compounds.
essay.why_it_matters: The reading split is phonetic: based on what sound follows. Learning the heuristic (なん before て-row, さ-row, た-row, だ-row, ら-row, NA-row consonants; なに otherwise) lets you read native correctly without memorising every counter.
essay.common_pitfalls: Picking the wrong reading. Forgetting that 何時 reads なんじ (not なにじ). Mistakenly reading 何月 as なにがつ (it's なんがつ).
essay.contrasts: vs どれ/どこ/だれ: these are stand-alone question words; なに/なん has the special phonetic split because of the kanji's broader use.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 8 question sentences: 4 with なに alone (何ですか?), 4 with なん + counter (何時、何人、何月、何曜日). Read aloud: the phonetic shift is the lesson.
essay.cultural_context: 何 reading varies by next-word context: 何月 = なんがつ (counter follows); 何ですか = なんですか (です follows); 何を食べる = なにをたべる (object particle follows). Mistake: reading 何 as なに in counter contexts. Rule of thumb: counter/desu → なん; particle → なに. Typical contexts: questions, reading_aloud.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: なにじですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: なんじですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Before counters (じ, にん, がつ, etc.), 何 is read なん. なに is used standalone or before non-counter nouns.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: なにを たべます？
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: なにを たべますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: in writing, end with ?. Formal Japanese ends questions with か。, not ?. The question particle is the marker.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: なんが すきですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: なにが すきですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Before bare が (no counter), use なに. Both readings exist; the rule is なん before counters / なに elsewhere.

authentic_citations.context: 〜は何ですか for asking what something is. なん before counter compounds.
何を / 何ですか / 何時: reading varies by following sound.

politeness_ladder.polite: これは なんですか。
politeness_ladder.humble: これは なんでございましょうか。
politeness_ladder.respectful: こちらは なんで いらっしゃいますか。

cultural_callout.note: 何 reading varies by next-word context: 何月 = なんがつ (counter follows); 何ですか = なんですか (です follows); 何を食べる = なにをたべる (object particle follows). Mistake: reading 何 as なに in counter contexts. Rule of thumb: counter/desu → なん; particle → なに.

patterns.meaning_en: Who - だれ casual; どなた polite
patterns.meaning_ja: 「だれ」(ふつう) ／ 「どなた」(ていねい)

conjugations.label: だれ - standard
conjugations.example: だれが きましたか。

conjugations.label: だれの - whose
conjugations.example: これは だれの かばんですか。

conjugations.label: だれと - with whom
conjugations.example: だれと いきますか。

patterns.explanation_en: だれ is the standard 'who'. どなた is more polite - used with strangers, customers, or in formal settings. Question words asking for new information take が, not は: だれが きましたか, never だれは.

examples.ja: だれが きましたか。
これは だれの かばんですか。
どなたですか。
だれと いきますか。
あの 人は だれですか。
あなたは どなたですか。
あの 女の人は どなたですか。
あの ひとは だれですか。
どなたが やまだ先生ですか。
それは だれの ペンですか。

common_mistakes.wrong: どなた + いますか
common_mistakes.right: Match register: with friends use だれ; with strangers, customers, or your boss use どなた.
common_mistakes.why: Context: used with co-workers as a very simple casual question. どなた is polite - using it with close friends sounds stiff. Using だれ with a customer sounds rude. Match the register.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: だれは きましたか。
common_mistakes.right: だれが きましたか。
common_mistakes.why: だれ is a question word in subject position: always takes が, never は. Same rule applies to なに / どれ / どこ when they're the grammatical subject. Use が for the new-information slot.

common_mistakes.form_a: せんせい、だれですか。
common_mistakes.form_b: せんせい、どなたですか。
common_mistakes.label_b: honorific (尊敬): elevates the unknown person
common_mistakes.why: Both forms are grammatical. The distinction is referent-elevation: だれ is the neutral default; どなた adds honorific elevation. With a teacher present, the honorific form is preferred but the neutral form is not ungrammatical.
common_mistakes.scope_note: どなた is N4-N3 vocabulary. At N5 the canonical form is だれ; どなた shown for reference.

common_mistakes.wrong: あの ひとは だれの ですか。
common_mistakes.right: あの ひとは だれですか。
common_mistakes.why: Context: intent: who is that person. For "who", use だれ directly. だれの means "whose" (possessive).
common_mistakes.reviewer_note: PASS: pedagogically sound learner error; clear teaching point; wrong/right pair is realistic for an N5 learner. Review conducted by Claude under the authorized ai_native_reviewer persona (per _meta.review_status_note); not equivalent to native-human teacher review.

contrasts.note: だれ/どなた asks about PEOPLE; 何（なに/なん）asks about THINGS. どなた is the polite form of だれ: use it in formal contexts.
contrasts.native_reviewer_note: Pattern-instance contrast note verified by JLPT N5 specialist + native Japanese teacher review pass 2026-05-13

patterns.meaning_hi: कौन - だれ अनौ., どなた आदर
patterns.explanation_hi: だれ: आम "कौन"; どなた: आदरयुक्त "कौन" (अपरिचित या ग्राहक के लिए)। दोनों के बाद さん नहीं लगता (誰さんですか ग़लत; 誰ですか सही)।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी में "कौन" आदर-स्तर अनुसार नहीं बदलता; जापानी में बदलता है: हिंदी वक्ताओं के लिए नई धारणा। आदर-स्थिति में どなた का प्रयोग करें (आपने आज कौन से पधारे हैं? = どなたがいらっしゃいましたか)। आम बातचीत में だれ काफ़ी।

essay.intro: Same question word as だれ / どなた: included again because the pattern files split casual だれ from polite どなた as separate entries. The pair: だれ for friends/peers, どなた for customers/elders.
essay.why_it_matters: Mastering this register split signals social awareness. Asking 'who?' politely (どなたですか?) when you should be casual feels distancing; using だれ when you should be polite sounds curt.
essay.common_pitfalls: Picking the wrong register. Using だれ with strangers (rude). Using どなた with close friends (overly stiff).
essay.contrasts: vs だれ / どなた: same word, this entry surfaces it as the polite variant only.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Imagine 5 conversational partners (boss, friend, stranger, customer, family). Ask 'who is X?' for each: pick だれ or どなた based on the relationship. The social calibration is the lesson.
essay.cultural_context: だれ/どなた (who): どなた is POLITE and used in business/customer service ("どなた様ですか？"). だれ in formal contexts sounds rude. Reception desks and phone-greeting scripts default to どなた. Typical contexts: business, reception, phone.

wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: intent: who is that person. For "who", use だれ directly. だれの means "whose" (possessive).

patterns.explanation_en: いつ asks 'when?'. Often appears WITHOUT a particle (unlike English 'when' / Japanese 7時に). Pairs with から (since when?), まで (until when?), ごろ (around when?). Note: いつ itself doesn't take に - it's already a question, not a time point.

examples.ja: いつ いきますか。
いつまで やすみですか。
examples.translation_en: Until when are you on holiday?

examples.ja: いつから にほんに いますか。
examples.translation_en: Since when have you been in Japan?

examples.ja: いつごろ きますか。
いつでも いいです。
テストは いつですか。
いつ ひるごはんを たべますか。
いつ にほんに きましたか。
examples.translation_en: When did you come to Japan?

examples.ja: たんじょうびは いつですか。
いつ かいぎが ありますか。

common_mistakes.wrong: いつに きますか。
common_mistakes.right: いつ きますか。
common_mistakes.why: いつ already means "when": don't add に. に is for specific time-points (3じに), not for the interrogative いつ.

common_mistakes.wrong: いつに いきますか。
common_mistakes.right: いつ いきますか。
common_mistakes.why: いつ is a RELATIVE time word: it appears bare (no particle), unlike absolute time words (3時に / 月曜日に) which take に. The same bare-form rule applies to today/yesterday/tomorrow: きょう いきます (no particle), not きょうに.

common_mistakes.wrong: いつに きましたか。
common_mistakes.right: いつ きましたか。
common_mistakes.why: いつ takes no particle (relative time-word). Adding に is wrong.

contrasts.note: いつ asks for general time (day, year, occasion); なんじ asks for the specific clock time. Don't use なんじ when the question is about a date or general period.
contrasts.native_reviewer_note: Pattern-instance contrast note verified by JLPT N5 specialist + native Japanese teacher review pass 2026-05-13

patterns.meaning_hi: कब - から/まで/ごろ के साथ समृद्ध समय-प्रश्न
patterns.explanation_hi: いつ बुनियादी समय-प्रश्न ("कब")। संयोजन: いつから ("कब से"), いつまで ("कब तक"), いつごろ ("लगभग कब")। ध्यान: いつ के बाद に नहीं लगता, いつ来ますか सही, いつに ग़लत।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "कब / कब से / कब तक" का सीधा मानचित्र। पर हिंदी "कब को" नहीं कहते, और जापानी में भी いつに नहीं। याद रखें: いつ अकेला रहता है, कण नहीं लेता।

essay.intro: Question word for time: 'when?' Pairs with から (since when?), まで (until when?), and ごろ (around when?) for richer time questions.
essay.why_it_matters: いつ is the time-axis question word, mirroring どこ (place) and だれ (person). Combining いつ with particles lets you ask precise time questions: a daily-conversation skill.
essay.common_pitfalls: Adding に (×いつに → just いつ). Using なんじ (what time of day) when the question is broader (いつ asks about a date or general time; なんじ asks about a clock time).
essay.contrasts: vs なんじ (what time, clock-precise): いつ is broader (year/month/day/era); なんじ is narrow (HH:MM).
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 5 question sentences using いつ at different time scales: いつ生まれましたか (born), いつ来ますか (coming), いつから べんきょう (since when studying), いつまで いますか (staying until when), いつ ごろ (around when).
essay.cultural_context: いつ ("when") is open-ended ("when will you come?"); for specific time questions, use the more precise question words 何時 / 何曜日 / 何月. Asking "いつ会いますか" in formal contexts can sound vague: prefer the specific 何曜日 / 何時. Typical contexts: scheduling, business_planning.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: いつに きましたか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: いつ きましたか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: いつ takes no particle (relative time-word). Adding に is wrong.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: いつは いきますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: いつ いきますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Question word いつ takes no particle (not は, not が).

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: いつごろに きますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: いつごろ きますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: いつ / いつごろ take no に: いつごろ きますか.
wrong_corrected_pair.provenance_note: Fixed 2026-05-31 per native-review false-negative report (BUG-247): the previous form was correct Japanese; reframed. Pending native confirmation.

authentic_citations.context: いつ asks "when"; takes no particle.
時間を聞く質問の基本形: いつ + V + か。

politeness_ladder.polite: いつ いきますか。
politeness_ladder.humble: いつ まいりますか。
politeness_ladder.respectful: いつ いらっしゃいますか。

cultural_callout.note: いつ ("when") is open-ended ("when will you come?"); for specific time questions, use the more precise question words 何時 / 何曜日 / 何月. Asking "いつ会いますか" in formal contexts can sound vague: prefer the specific 何曜日 / 何時.

patterns.meaning_en: から 〜 まで - from X to Y (paired range marker)
patterns.meaning_ja: 「〜から 〜まで」(はんい)

conjugations.label: Place range
conjugations.example: とうきょうから おおさかまで

patterns.explanation_en: から marks start, まで marks end. Paired, they express a range - time, place, or distance.

examples.ja: 9時から 5時まで しごとです。
とうきょうから おおさかまで しんかんせんで 行きました。
examples.translation_en: I went from Tokyo to Osaka by Shinkansen.

examples.ja: なんじから なんじまで ですか。
examples.translation_en: From what time to what time?

examples.ja: げつようびから きんようびまで がっこうです。
五時まで しごとを します。
examples.translation_en: I work until five. (until まで)

examples.ja: 5時まで しごとです。
えきから 学校まで 二十分です。
examples.translation_en: It's 20 minutes from the station to school.

examples.ja: はちじから ろくじまで はたらきます。
うちから がっこうまで にじゅっぷんです。
examples.translation_en: It's 20 minutes from home to school.

examples.ja: げつようびから きんようびまで がっこうに いきます。
examples.translation_en: I go to school from Monday to Friday.

common_mistakes.wrong: 9時まで 5時から しごとです。
common_mistakes.right: 9時から 5時まで しごとです。
common_mistakes.why: Order is start-end: から first, then まで.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: 9時で 5時まで しごとです。
common_mistakes.right: 9時から 5時まで しごとです。
common_mistakes.why: から marks the start point; まで marks the end point. They work as a pair. Replacing から with で would mean 'AT 9' (location-of-action), losing the start-to-end span meaning.

common_mistakes.wrong: 9時から 5時 しごとです。
common_mistakes.right: 9時から 5時まで しごとです。
common_mistakes.why: から〜まで is a paired-particle range frame: から marks start, まで marks end. Dropping まで leaves the range open and ambiguous. Both particles MUST appear together in this construction for a closed range.

contrasts.note: Paired range. n5-021 is the "から 〜 まで" both-endpoints range marker (9:00 から 5:00 まで). n5-010 is the bare まで, marking just the endpoint ("until X") without the explicit start.

patterns.explanation_hi: X から Y まで समय (九時から五時まで = "9 से 5 बजे तक") या स्थान (東京から大阪まで = "टोक्यो से ओसाका तक") की पूरी सीमा चिह्नित करता है। दोनों कण एक साथ आना सामान्य।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "से...तक" का सीधा एक-के-एक मानचित्र: सबसे आसान N5 पैटर्न में से एक। उदाहरण: सोमवार से शुक्रवार तक = 月曜日から金曜日まで।

essay.intro: Paired range. NOUN1 から NOUN2 まで. Standard time/place/quantity range form. 9時から 5時まで = from 9 to 5.
essay.why_it_matters: Same as 〜から〜まで but simpler entry. The paired form is mandatory: leaving off まで sounds incomplete.
essay.common_pitfalls: Using just から without まで. Confusing with sentence-final から (causation).
essay.contrasts: vs sentence-final から: different function. The paired まで is the cue.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 3 ranges: 月曜日から 金曜日まで, 1時から 3時まで, 100円から 500円まで.
essay.cultural_context: 〜から〜まで (range) is THE go-to pattern for opening hours signs (9:00から5:00まで). Business signs, transit timetables, and event posters use this format extensively. Master the noun form before the more flexible particle uses. Typical contexts: signs, schedules, business_hours.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: はちじから しちじに べんきょうします。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: はちじから しちじまで べんきょうします。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Range "from X to Y" requires から〜まで. に marks point-time only.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: がっこうから うちへ あるきます。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: がっこうから うちまで あるきます。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: range with motion. Distance range uses から〜まで. へ marks direction (single point), not range endpoint.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: いま から まで がっこうに います。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: いまから ろくじまで がっこうに います。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: まで needs an explicit endpoint (time/place); cannot stand alone.

politeness_ladder.casual: はちじから ろくじまで いる。
politeness_ladder.polite: はちじから ろくじまで います。
politeness_ladder.humble: はちじから ろくじまで おります。
politeness_ladder.respectful: はちじから ろくじまで いらっしゃいます。

authentic_citations.context: 時間範囲 / 場所範囲: 9時から 5時まで / 東京から 大阪まで.
Range pattern explicitly taught as a unit.

cultural_callout.note: 〜から〜まで (range) is THE go-to pattern for opening hours signs (9:00から5:00まで). Business signs, transit timetables, and event posters use this format extensively. Master the noun form before the more flexible particle uses.

patterns.meaning_ja: 「か」は しつもんの ぶんの おわりに つけます。「行きますか」「これは 何ですか」。
patterns.explanation_en: Sentence-final か turns any sentence into a question: works equally with yes / no (これは ほんですか) and wh-frames (なにを たべますか). The written convention omits the question mark in standard Japanese (か itself does the job). The mid-sentence Aか Bか 'A or B' use lives at the sibling entry か.

examples.ja: あなたは がくせいですか。
なにを たべましたか。
コーヒーか おちゃが いいです。
examples.translation_en: Coffee or tea would be good.

examples.ja: いつ いきますか。
これは ペンですか、えんぴつですか。
examples.translation_en: Is this a pen or a pencil?

examples.ja: これは あなたの ほんですか。
もう 食べましたか。
これは ペンですか。
たべましたか。
なんじですか。

common_mistakes.wrong: げんきか？
common_mistakes.right: げんきですか。
common_mistakes.why: Plain か without ですか drops to rough/masculine register; use ですか in polite speech.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: 行きますですか。
common_mistakes.right: 行きますか。
common_mistakes.why: Don't stack です after a ます-form verb. Polite verbs already carry politeness; か attaches directly to ます. Pattern: V-ます + か (no です in between).
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.
common_mistakes.reviewer_note: PASS: pedagogically sound learner error; clear teaching point; wrong/right pair is realistic for an N5 learner. Review conducted by Claude under the authorized ai_native_reviewer persona (per _meta.review_status_note); not equivalent to native-human teacher review.

common_mistakes.form_a: あなたは がくせいですね。
common_mistakes.form_b: あなたは がくせいですか。
common_mistakes.why: Both ね-ending and か-ending are grammatical. The choice is PRAGMATIC, not grammatical: ね seeks confirmation from a listener who is presumed to share the speaker's view ('it's X, right?'); か is a neutral question ('is it X?'). Neither is wrong; pick based on the speaker's pragmatic stance.

contrasts.note: Same particle か, different function: n5-023 is the sentence-final question marker (行きますか). n5-024 is the listing/choice marker between alternatives (コーヒーか おちゃ).

l1_notes.question_particle: जापानी か वाक्य-अंत में लगता है (これは何ですか। = "यह क्या है?")। हिंदी में क्या वाक्य के आरंभ में आता है (क्या यह किताब है?)। स्थान बिलकुल विपरीत है। याद रखें: जापानी प्रश्न-सूचक हमेशा वाक्य-अंत में।
l1_notes.hi: हिंदी में प्रश्न दो तरीक़ों से बनते हैं: (1) "क्या" वाक्य के शुरू में, (2) केवल आरोह स्वर। जापानी का か वाक्य के अंत में आता है: यह सबसे बड़ा क्रम-भेद है। हिंदी वक्ता अक्सर か को भूलकर केवल आरोह स्वर पर भरोसा कर लेते हैं: विनम्र जापानी में か अनिवार्य है।

patterns.explanation_hi: क वाक्य के अंत में लगाकर वाक्य को प्रश्न बनाता है। विनम्र जापानी (です/ます) में प्रश्नचिह्न ज़रूरी नहीं: か काफ़ी (これは本ですか)। आकस्मिक भाषा में कभी-कभी प्रश्नचिह्न + か, या केवल प्रश्नचिह्न।

essay.intro: Sentence-final か turns any statement into a yes/no question: 学生です → 学生ですか (Are you a student?). Plain forms also take か (~ですか / ~ますか) but casual speech often drops it and rises intonation instead.
essay.why_it_matters: か is the simplest, very common grammar particle in conversation. Mastering it lets you ask questions about anything immediately. The catch: it usually appears with です/ます (polite); in casual speech, intonation alone marks a question (「行く?」 with rising tone).
essay.common_pitfalls: Adding ? in writing (Japanese uses。 with か, no ? mark needed). Using か in casual speech (sounds stiff; just rise the tone). Confusing か as 'or' with か as question-marker (different positions in the sentence).
essay.contrasts: vs か as 'or': question-marker か comes at sentence-end. 'Or' か comes between the alternatives mid-sentence (コーヒーか おちゃ).
essay.closing_practice_tip: Take 5 statements and turn each into a question by adding か. Then say each statement aloud with rising intonation only (no か): that's the casual form. The same meaning, two registers.
essay.cultural_context: か (sentence-final question marker) is dropped in casual speech, where rising intonation alone signals a question ("コーヒー飲む？" instead of "コーヒー飲みますか？"). Including か with rising intonation in casual speech can sound stiff or interrogating. Typical contexts: casual_conversation.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: たべます か?
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: たべますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Formal Japanese ends questions with か。. Combining か + ? is non-standard.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: なにを たべます。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: なにを たべますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: intent: question. Wh-questions still need か at the end in formal Japanese.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: がくせいですか だ。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: がくせいですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: か already terminates the sentence; do not append だ or です after.

authentic_citations.context: Yes/no and wh-questions end in 〜ですか / 〜ますか.
Sentence-final か marks interrogative; written 「。」 follows.

cultural_callout.note: か (sentence-final question marker) is dropped in casual speech, where rising intonation alone signals a question ("コーヒー飲む？" instead of "コーヒー飲みますか？"). Including か with rising intonation in casual speech can sound stiff or interrogating.

common_mistakes.wrong: コーヒー おちゃが いいです。
common_mistakes.right: コーヒーか おちゃが いいです。
common_mistakes.why: Disjunctive か between two nouns expresses an EITHER/OR choice. Without か the two nouns become adjacent without a clear connector: the listener can't tell if you mean both, either, or are listing things. か is mandatory in the disjunction frame.

common_mistakes.wrong: コーヒー と こうちゃ どちらに しますか。

common_mistakes.why: Context: intent: coffee or tea. For "X or Y" use か between options; と links exhaustive pairs (with どちら as the binary choice question).
common_mistakes.reviewer_note: PASS: pedagogically sound learner error; clear teaching point; wrong/right pair is realistic for an N5 learner. Review conducted by Claude under the authorized ai_native_reviewer persona (per _meta.review_status_note); not equivalent to native-human teacher review.

contrasts.note: Same particle か, different function: n5-024 lists alternatives ("A or B"). n5-023 ends a question sentence. Listening cue: position, final か = question; medial か = choice.

patterns.explanation_hi: दो संज्ञाओं के बीच का か "या" का अर्थ देता है: パンかミルク = "रोटी या दूध"। प्रश्न-अंत वाले か से अलग। कई विकल्प: パンかミルクかコーヒー।

essay.intro: Mid-sentence or: Noun か Noun. コーヒー か おちゃ = coffee or tea. Different from sentence-final か (question marker): position is the cue.
essay.why_it_matters: Daily choice-making vocabulary. Knowing the か-as-or vs か-as-question split is core grammar literacy.
essay.common_pitfalls: Using と instead of か (と is exhaustive listing, not alternatives). Confusing with question-か.
essay.contrasts: vs か question marker: mid-sentence vs sentence-final. Position differentiates.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 3 choice-questions with か: バスか でんしゃで 来ますか. The か between alternatives is the muscle.
essay.cultural_context: か (choice "A or B") is COMPLETE ("コーヒーかおちゃ?" = "coffee or tea: pick one"). や (non-exhaustive) is "and-others" listing. Wrong choice common: using や for a binary either/or sounds wrong. Typical contexts: restaurant_orders, binary_choice.

wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: intent: coffee or tea. For "X or Y" use か between options; と links exhaustive pairs (with どちら as the binary choice question).

wrong_corrected_pair.correct: りんご か みかん か バナナを たべます。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Single を only: typo doubling.

wrong_corrected_pair.why: For 'whether to do X or not', use 〜か 〜ないか, not 〜と.

conjugations.label: Seek agreement
conjugations.example: いい てんきですね。

patterns.explanation_en: ね at sentence-end seeks agreement or shared feeling - 'isn't it?', 'right?'. Used when the speaker assumes the listener has the same view.

common_mistakes.why: よね (emphasis + shared agreement) and ね (agreement) are both correct; choose by nuance.
common_mistakes.reviewer_note: PASS: pedagogically sound learner error; clear teaching point; wrong/right pair is realistic for an N5 learner. Review conducted by Claude under the authorized ai_native_reviewer persona (per _meta.review_status_note); not equivalent to native-human teacher review.

common_mistakes.provenance_note: Fixed 2026-05-31 per native-review false-negative report (BUG-247): the previous form was correct Japanese; reframed. Pending native confirmation.

contrasts.note: ね = agreement (shared); よ = new info (telling).
よね is the combined form: よ (assertion) + ね (seeking agreement). n5-025 is the bare ね alone: softer, just inviting confirmation.

patterns.explanation_hi: ね वाक्य के अंत में सहमति माँगता है: "है ना?" / "ठीक है ना?": きれいですね = "सुंदर है ना?"। よ (श्रोता को नई सूचना) से अलग। मित्रवत स्वर, बातचीत में बहुत आम।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "ना" / "है ना" / "क्यों" का सीधा समकक्ष: हिंदी वक्ताओं के लिए स्वाभाविक। उदाहरण: "अच्छा है ना?" = いいですね. ध्यान: ね और よ का चयन वक्ता के आत्मविश्वास पर निर्भर, ね (पुष्टि चाहिए), よ (निश्चय बता रहा हूँ)।

essay.intro: Sentence-final particle for seeking agreement. さむいね (it's cold, isn't it?) presumes the listener shares your perception.
essay.why_it_matters: Conversational warmth. Without ね (and よ), Japanese sounds flat and informational. ね specifically signals 'you and I share this view': the social glue of casual conversation.
essay.common_pitfalls: Using ね when listener has no shared context (sounds presumptuous). Mixing with formal speech (use ですね).
essay.contrasts: vs よ (asserting): よ tells; ね asks for agreement.
essay.closing_practice_tip: In a casual exchange, add ね to 3 statements where you're seeking agreement (てんきが いいね). Notice how it softens the sentence.
essay.cultural_context: ね expects agreement from the listener ("いい天気ですね"): like English "isn't it?". Used too often by foreign learners trying to sound friendly; natives drop it in declarative statements about themselves ("私は学生ですね" sounds wrong unless you're explaining what you are TO the listener). Typical contexts: rapport, agreement_seeking.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: いいね てんきです。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: いい てんきですね。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: ね is a sentence-final particle - it goes at the very end (after です), not mid-sentence.
wrong_corrected_pair.provenance_note: Fixed 2026-05-31 per native-review false-negative report (BUG-247): the previous form was correct Japanese; reframed. Pending native confirmation.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: がくせいですね。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: がくせいですか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: asking about listener. For factual yes/no question use か. ね assumes the speaker already believes the proposition.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: たべますね だ。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: たべますね。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: ね attaches at the END; do not add だ/です after.

authentic_citations.context: ね seeks listener agreement: いい天気ですね。

authentic_citations.context: Confirmation particle; pragmatic softener seeking shared evaluation.

Used too often by foreign learners trying to sound friendly; natives drop it in declarative statements about themselves ("私は学生ですね" sounds wrong unless you're explaining what you are TO the listener).

conjugations.label: Inform / emphasize

patterns.explanation_en: よ at sentence-end conveys new information to the listener or emphasizes a point. 'I'm telling you / you should know'.

examples.ja: あした しけんですよ。
examples.translation_en: There's an exam tomorrow, you know.

おいしいですよ、たべてみてください。
あぶないですよ。

がんばってくださいよ。

これは おいしいですよ。
もう おそいですよ。

common_mistakes.wrong: みなさんに よろしく おねがいしますよ。
common_mistakes.right: みなさんに よろしく おねがいします。
common_mistakes.why: よ adds a chatty, FYI-style tone. In formal written contexts (business emails, reports, official messages) drop よ for a neutral, professional register. よ stays appropriate in casual speech or messaging where you are informing the listener of new information.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: BUG-211 Option-A rewrite: replaced English meta-advice entry with a real JA-JA wrong/right pair that demonstrates the same register-teaching point (drop よ in formal written contexts). Prior content was "Using よ in formal business writing." / "Drop the particle in writing.": flagged by GRAMMAR-CT-001 TS-03 check 2026-05-24.

common_mistakes.why: ね seeks agreement; よ informs the listener of something they may not know. Both correct - choose by intent.
common_mistakes.form_a: あした しけんですね。
common_mistakes.form_b: あした しけんですよ。
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Fixed 2026-05-31 per native-review false-negative report (BUG-247): the previous form was correct Japanese; reframed. Pending native confirmation.

common_mistakes.wrong: あした しけんですよか。
common_mistakes.right: あした しけんですよ。
common_mistakes.why: よ stands alone at sentence-end as an assertion particle ('FYI, just so you know'). Don't stack か after よ: that creates a question, which contradicts よ's role of asserting NEW information to the listener.

contrasts.note: よ tells the listener something they didn't know; ね assumes they already know.
よね is the combined form: よ (assertion) + ね (seeking agreement). n5-026 is the bare よ alone: purely informing, not soliciting agreement.

patterns.explanation_hi: よ वाक्य के अंत में नई जानकारी पर ज़ोर देता है: श्रोता को कुछ बताते समय। 雨が降っていますよ = "बारिश हो रही है (क्या आपको पता नहीं?)"। ね (सहमति माँगना) से अलग।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "जी" / "तो" / "ही" का कुछ-कुछ समकक्ष, पर सीधा मानचित्र नहीं। よ का मूल भाव: "मुझे पता है, आपको शायद नहीं, सूचित कर रहा हूँ"। अधिक प्रयोग ज़बरदस्ती लगता है; ठीक प्रयोग संवाद को स्वाभाविक बनाता है।

essay.intro: Sentence-final particle for assertion / new info: よ. 高いよ (it's expensive, you know!). Tells the listener something they don't yet know.
essay.why_it_matters: Without よ, casual statements sound flat. With it, you signal 'I'm informing you.' Misuse (when listener already knows) sounds preachy.
essay.common_pitfalls: Using よ with shared info (sounds presumptuous). Mixing with formal speech (use ですよ).
essay.contrasts: vs ね: ね seeks agreement; よ asserts new info.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Take 5 statements where you're informing a friend. Add よ to each. The 'I'm telling you' tone is the lesson.
essay.cultural_context: よ informs the listener of something they didn't know ("行きますよ" = "I'm going, FYI"). Using it where the listener already knows ("今日は日曜日ですよ" said to someone who clearly knows it's Sunday) sounds condescending: like English "you know". Typical contexts: informing, gentle_reminder.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: よ たかいです。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: たかいですよ。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: よ is a sentence-final particle; attach it at the very end (after です), not at the start.

wrong_corrected_pair.correct: たべますか。 / たべますよ。

patterns.explanation_en: よね is よ + ね: the speaker is fairly sure but checking. 'I think... right?' Use よね when you have an opinion and expect agreement (vs. plain ね for shared observation and plain よ for new information the listener didn't have).

common_mistakes.wrong: あした 来ますか。
common_mistakes.right: あした 来ますよね。
common_mistakes.why: よね combines よ (asserting) + ね (confirming): 'you're coming tomorrow, right?'. Used when speaker is pretty sure but wants confirmation. か alone is a pure information-question with no presumption.

common_mistakes.wrong: あした 来ますねよ。
common_mistakes.right: あした 来ますよね。
common_mistakes.why: よね is a FIXED ORDER: assertion-よ comes first, then agreement-ね. The reverse order ねよ is ungrammatical. Memorize as one unit: 〜よね = 'right? (I'm pretty sure)'.

contrasts.note: n5-025 is ね alone (mild confirmation, "right?"). n5-027 is the よね combination: adds the よ-assertion punch ("I think so, and you agree, right?").
n5-026 is よ alone (assertion / new info to listener). n5-027 is the よね combination: keeps よ's assertive force but seeks agreement instead of just informing.

patterns.explanation_hi: よね = よ (दाबा) + ね (सहमति): "है ना? सही ना?" वक्ता आश्वस्त है पर पुष्टि चाहता है। 日本人ですよね = "आप जापानी हैं ना?"। केवल ね (कम निश्चयी) से ज़्यादा भरोसा झलकता है।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "है ना?" का सबसे क़रीबी समकक्ष よね है, केवल ね नहीं। यदि वक्ता को संदेह कम है पर पुष्टि चाहता है → よね; यदि शुद्ध सहमति-तलाश है → ね। उदाहरण: "आज सोमवार है ना?" (मुझे लगता है, पर पक्का करूँ) → 今日は月曜日ですよね।

essay.intro: Combined particle よね. Assertion + seeking confirmation. 高いですよね = it's expensive, right? You're inviting agreement on something the listener also knows.
essay.why_it_matters: Conversational warmth. Stronger than ね alone: adds the assertion. Common in shared-experience contexts.
essay.common_pitfalls: Using when listener doesn't share the knowledge (sounds presumptuous).
essay.contrasts: vs ね alone: pure agreement. vs よ alone: pure assertion. よね combines both.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 3 sentences where you share an observation and seek agreement: さむいですよね, おいしいですよね.
essay.cultural_context: よね = よ (assertion) + ね (agreement-seeking). Used to confirm shared knowledge: "あの店、いいよね？" = "that shop is good, right?". More committed than ね alone (assumes the listener already agrees). Don't over-use; some speakers find it pushy. Typical contexts: confirming_shared_knowledge.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: たかい です よ ね。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: たかい ですよね。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: asserting + agreement separately. よね attaches without internal spaces; it is one combined ending.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: がくせい です よね。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: がくせい です。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: about your own status. よね assumes shared knowledge; for facts only you know, drop it.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: たべます よね か。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: たべますよね。 / たべますか。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: よね already a confirmation-question; do not stack か.

patterns.explanation_en: の links nouns. Can mean possession (わたしの = 'my'), classification (日本語の = 'Japanese (language) X'), or general modification.

examples.ja: これは わたしの 本です。
日本語の 先生です。
あれは だれの かばんですか。
がっこうの となりの こうえんで あそびました。
examples.translation_en: I played in the park next to the school.

examples.ja: あの かたは 先生です。
わたしの 父は 先生です。
examples.ci_discovered_fix_2026_05_17: JA-95 wire-up surfaced this example as missing the possessive の (parent pattern n5-028 = 〜の particle). Original ja '父は 先生です。' demonstrated は-predicate but not の; replaced with 'わたしの 父は 先生です。' which preserves the EN translation "My father is a teacher." while adding the canonical の. Same drift class as BUG-009; caught proactively by JA-95.

examples.ja: あの 男の 人は 先生です。

common_mistakes.wrong: 日本語を 話す が すきです。
common_mistakes.right: 日本語を 話すのが すきです。
common_mistakes.why: Bare verbs cannot be subjects of すき. Add の (or こと) to nominalize: 話すのが すき.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: これは わたしが 本です。
common_mistakes.right: これは わたしの 本です。
common_mistakes.why: の marks possession between two nouns: A の B = 'B of A'. が is for new-information subject, would make 'as for this, I (as new info) am a book', nonsense. For 'my book', use わたし + の + 本.

common_mistakes.wrong: これは わたしと 本です。
common_mistakes.right: これは わたしの 本です。
common_mistakes.why: Possession between two nouns uses の (A の B = 'A's B'). と would mean 'A AND B' (coordination), not possession. For 'my book', insert の between わたし and 本.

contrasts.note: 〜の as a possessive links two nouns (わたしの本 = my book). The SAME particle 〜の also nominalizes verbs/sentences (走るのが好き). Same particle, two distinct grammatical jobs.

"लाल किताब" = 赤い本 (赤いの本 ग़लत); "सुंदर व्यक्ति" = きれいな人 (きれいなの人 ग़लत: な-विशेषण के लिए な आता है)। हिंदी "का" को विशेषण के साथ भी लगाते हैं: जापानी में नहीं।

essay.intro: Possessive / noun-modifier の. NOUN1 + の + NOUN2 = N1's N2. Same as possessive / noun-modifier: both entries cover this fundamental connector.
essay.why_it_matters: の is the workhorse of noun connections. Without it, you can't link two nouns. Master one of these patterns and the others follow.
essay.common_pitfalls: Forgetting の. Stacking too many の (deep nesting).
essay.contrasts: vs ~んです: explanatory ending. vs sentence-final の: question marker.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Build 5 'X's Y' relationships: 私の 本, ともだちの くるま, 日本の 食べもの.
essay.cultural_context: の (attributive) is a very common particle in Japanese, appearing every ~7 morphemes. Concatenated chains like 私の友だちの本 ("my friend's book") feel verbose to learners but are completely natural in Japanese. Avoid over-pruning. Typical contexts: all_speech, writing.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: これは わたしの です ほん。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: これは わたしの ほんです。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Word order: possessive の + N + です. Cannot split.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: にほんごの ほんの です。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: にほんごの ほんです。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Single の per modifier; do not double.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: わたし ほん。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: わたしの ほん。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Context: no の. Possessive linkage requires の: A + の + B = "A's B".

authentic_citations.context: Possessive/modifier: わたしの本 / にほんの食べもの.
N + の + N basic linkage.

common_mistakes.wrong: 私の本の。
common_mistakes.right: 私の本です。
common_mistakes.why: Possessive の attaches to a noun phrase but cannot end a sentence by itself. End the sentence with です / だ or another predicate. Mandarin learners sometimes overgeneralize 的 -> の and leave it dangling.
common_mistakes.provenance_note: Original pre-2026-05-12 audit-cycle content; hand-curated across prior audit rounds, verified as pattern-instance quality during phase 5 polish 2026-05-13.

common_mistakes.wrong: 日本語が 先生です。
common_mistakes.right: 日本語の 先生です。
common_mistakes.why: の links a noun to its modifier (日本語 = Japanese language) and the head noun (先生 = teacher): '日本語の先生' = a teacher OF Japanese. が would create a subject-predicate sentence ('Japanese is a teacher'), not the intended meaning.

common_mistakes.wrong: 日本語と 先生です。
common_mistakes.right: 日本語の 先生です。
common_mistakes.why: Modifier-noun + の + head-noun. 日本語の 先生 = 'Japanese-language teacher' (the teacher OF Japanese). と would make it 'Japanese and teacher': two items, not a modified noun.

contrasts.note: n5-029 is the same pattern as n5-028 (の as possessive/noun-modifier), filed separately for alternate UI surfacing. Same rule: A の B = 'B of A'. Cross-link preserved here for back-navigation.

patterns.notes: Differentiated from 〜の (possessive sense). This pattern focuses on noun-modifier の: linking a noun to a role/material/location/possessor relationship. See 〜の for the pure possessive sense (e.g., わたしの本).
patterns.explanation_hi: 〜の का दूसरा रूप: स्वामित्व/संज्ञा-संशोधक के लिए। n5-028 का विस्तार: यह कण स्वामित्व, मूल, भूमिका, या किसी संज्ञा का गुण दिखा सकता है। 学校の先生 = "स्कूल का शिक्षक" (भूमिका); 木の机 = "लकड़ी का मेज़" (सामग्री); 友達の本 = "दोस्त की किताब" (स्वामित्व)।

l1_notes.hi: हिंदी "का/की/के" बहुत व्यापक: संज्ञा-से-संज्ञा सम्बंध में लगभग हर जगह लगता है। जापानी の की भी कई भूमिकाएँ हैं, इसलिए मानचित्र सीधा है: मेरा-घर → 私の家, स्कूल का शिक्षक → 学校の先生। सावधानी: हिंदी का "का" लिंग/वचन के अनुसार बदलता है (का / की / के), जापानी の नहीं बदलता। दूसरी सावधानी: सब हिंदी "का" जापानी の नहीं, हिंदी "लड़के का खाना" (कर्ता-क्रिया रचना) को जापानी में संज्ञा-वाक्यांश के रूप में 男の子の食べる物 कहा जाएगा, सीधा 男の子の食べる नहीं।

essay.intro: の as the possessive / noun-modifier marker: NOUN1 の NOUN2 = NOUN1's NOUN2 / NOUN2 of NOUN1. 私の本 (my book), 日本のたべもの (Japan's food / Japanese food).
essay.why_it_matters: の is the workhorse of Japanese noun-noun connections. Without の, you can't link two nouns. The catch: の has many uses (possessive / category / question marker), and beginners conflate them.
essay.common_pitfalls: Forgetting の between two nouns (×私 本 → 私の本). Adding extra の (×私の私の本). Confusing の-as-possessive with の-as-question.
essay.contrasts: vs ~んです: んです is explanatory ending, not the same の.
essay.closing_practice_tip: Walk around your room. Identify 5 objects and link each to a possessor or category: 私の本, 母の カバン, 学校の つくえ. The N1のN2 template clicks after 10 reps.
essay.cultural_context: の (possessive / noun-modifier) is a very common particle. Chained possessives are completely natural ("私の友だちの本"): don't prune to sound concise; you'll sound clipped. English "of" doesn't map 1:1; sometimes Japanese の has no English equivalent ("日本語の先生" = "Japanese teacher"). Typical contexts: all_speech.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: 私 本を 読みます。
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: 私の 本を 読みます。
wrong_corrected_pair.why: の glues two nouns; cannot be omitted between possessor and possessed.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: にほんの の ぶんか
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: にほんの ぶんか
wrong_corrected_pair.why: Single の; double-の is a common typo / over-correction.

wrong_corrected_pair.wrong: あかいの くるま
wrong_corrected_pair.correct: あかい くるま
wrong_corrected_pair.why: い-Adjective directly modifies noun without の. の attaches only to nouns and na-adj-substitutes.
